subject: packaging-coder-60

messages.content: You assign semantic types to the inputs and outputs of tools, so that tools can be chained: the output of one tool becomes the input of another. Reply with JSON only.

These tools come from one library:

### get_default_marker_environment
Return the default marker environment for the current Python process.
wraps packaging.markers.default_environment
- output, e.g. {"implementation_name": "cpython", "implementation_version": "3.12.3", "os_name": "posix", "platform_machine": "arm64", "platform_release": "27.2.0", "platfo...

### evaluate_marker
Evaluate a marker expression against an environment.
wraps packaging.markers.Marker.evaluate
- parameter `marker` (string), e.g. "python_version >= '3.6'", "sys_platform == 'win32'", "extra == 'dev'"
- parameter `environment` (null/object), e.g. {"sys_platform": "linux"}, {"extra": "dev"}, {"implementation_name": "pypy"}
- parameter `context` (null/string), e.g. "metadata", "requirement", "lock_file"
- output, e.g. true, false

### parse_metadata_email
Parse distribution metadata stored as email headers. data: Distribution metadata as email headers, e.g. 'Name: example
wraps packaging.metadata.parse_email
- parameter `data` (string), e.g. "Name: example-package\nVersion: 1.0.0\nSummary: An example package\n", "Name: test-package\nVersion: 2.0.0\nAuthor: John Doe\nAuthor-Email: john@example.com\nClassifier: Developm..., "Name: multi-value-test\nVersion: 1.0.0\nHome-Page: https://example.com\nHome-Page: https://another-example...
- output, e.g. {"core": {"name": "example-package", "version": "1.0.0", "summary": "An example package"}, "unparsed": {}}, {"core": {"name": "test-package", "version": "2.0.0", "author": "John Doe", "classifiers": ["Development Status :: 4 - Beta", "Intended Audience :: Developer..., {"core": {"name": "multi-value-test", "version": "1.0.0"}, "unparsed": {"home-page": ["https://example.com", "https://another-example.com"]}}

### create_empty_version_range
Return an empty version range that accepts no versions. prereleases: whether prereleases should be considered when determining if the range is empty -> the empt
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.empty
- parameter `prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. true, false
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '(empty)'>", "<VersionRange '(empty)' pre=True>", "<VersionRange '(empty)' pre=False>"

### create_full_version_range
Return a full version range that accepts all versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-rele
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.full
- parameter `admit_arbitrary` (boolean), e.g. true, false
- parameter `prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. true, false
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)' arbitrary>", "<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)'>", "<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)' arbitrary pre=True>"

### create_singleton_version_range
Return a version range that only accepts a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to 
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.singleton
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0.0", "2.0.0a1", "3.0.0+build.1"
- parameter `prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. true, false
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '[1.0.0, 1.0.0]'>", "<VersionRange '[2.0.0a1, 2.0.0a1]' pre=True>", "<VersionRange '[3.0.0+build.1, 3.0.0+build.1]' pre=False>"

### intersect_version_ranges
Compute the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. Example: intersect_version_ranges
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.intersection
- parameter `range1` (string), e.g. ">=1.0", ">1.0,<3.0", "==1.0.0"
- parameter `range2` (string), e.g. "<2.0", ">=2.0,<4.0", "==1.0.0"
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'>", "<VersionRange '[2.0, 3.0.dev0)'>", "<VersionRange '[1.0.0, 1.0.0[AFTER_LOCALS]]'>"

### union_version_ranges
Compute the union of two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format, version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format. Exampl
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.union
- parameter `version_range_a` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", "==1.0", ">=1.0"
- parameter `version_range_b` (string), e.g. ">=2.0,<3.0", "==2.0", "<2.0"
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '[1.0, 2.0.dev0) | [2.0, 3.0.dev0)'>", "<VersionRange '[1.0, 1.0[AFTER_LOCALS]] | [2.0, 2.0[AFTER_LOCALS]]'>", "<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)'>"

### complement_version_range
Compute the complement of a version range. version_specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0', '<2.0') -> The complement range as a string.
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.complement
- parameter `version_specifier` (string), e.g. ">=1.0", "<2.0", "==1.0.0"
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '(-inf, 1.0)'>", "<VersionRange '[2.0.dev0, +inf)'>", "<VersionRange '(-inf, 1.0.0) | (1.0.0[AFTER_LOCALS], +inf)'>"

### difference_version_ranges
Compute the difference between two version ranges. version_range_a: The first version range in specifier format (e.g., '>=1.0'), version_range_b: The second ver
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.difference
- parameter `version_range_a` (string), e.g. ">=1.0", ">=1.0,<3.0", "==1.0.0"
- parameter `version_range_b` (string), e.g. ">=2.0", ">=2.0,<3.0", "==1.0.0"
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '[1.0, 2.0)'>", "<VersionRange '(empty)'>"

### check_version_range_subset
Check if one version range is a subset of another. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier to check if range1 is a subset 
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.is_subset
- parameter `range1` (string), e.g. ">=1.5,<1.8", ">=1.0,<2.0", "==1.5.0"
- parameter `range2` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", ">=1.5,<1.8", "==1.5.0"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_version_range_superset
Check if one version range is a superset of another. outer_range: A version range specifier string for the outer range, inner_range: A version range specifier s
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.is_superset
- parameter `outer_range` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", ">=1.0,<3.0", "<2.0"
- parameter `inner_range` (string), e.g. ">=1.5,<1.8", ">=1.0,<2.0", ">=2.0,<3.0"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_version_ranges_disjoint
Check if two version ranges have no common elements. range1: First version range specifier, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Second version range specifier, e.g. '>=2
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.is_disjoint
- parameter `range1` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", ">=1.5,<2.5", "==1.0.0"
- parameter `range2` (string), e.g. ">=2.0,<3.0", ">=1.0,<2.0", ">=1.0.1"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_version_in_range
Check if a version is contained within a version range.
wraps packaging.ranges.VersionRange.contains
- parameter `specifier_set` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", "==1.0.0", ">=1.0"
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.5", "2.0", "0.9"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_unsatisfiable
- parameter `specifiers` (string), e.g. ">=2.0,<1.0", ">=1.0,<2.0", ""
- output, e.g. true, false

### convert_specifier_set_to_range
Convert a specifier set to a version range. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.to_range
- parameter `specifiers` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2.0", "", "===1.0.0"
- output, e.g. "<VersionRange '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'>", "<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)' arbitrary>", "<VersionRange '{1.0.0}'>"

### check_specifier_set_subset
Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. 
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_subset
- parameter `specifier_set1` (string), e.g. ">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12", "==3.12.0"
- parameter `specifier_set2` (string), e.g. ">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.9"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_specifier_set_superset
Check if one specifier set is a superset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_superset
- parameter `specifier_set1` (string), e.g. ">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.15", "==3.12.0"
- parameter `specifier_set2` (string), e.g. ">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12", "==3.12.0"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_specifier_sets_disjoint
Check if two specifier sets share no matching versions.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_disjoint
- parameter `specifier_set1` (string), e.g. "<3.12", ">=2.0,<3.0", "==1.0.0"
- parameter `specifier_set2` (string), e.g. ">=3.12", ">=3.11", ">3.0"
- output, e.g. true, false

### check_version_in_specifier_set
Check if a version is contained in a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representing the version specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The versi
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.contains
- parameter `specifier_set` (string), e.g. ">=1.0.0,!=1.0.1"
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.2.3", "1.0.1", "1.3.0a1"
- parameter `prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. false, true
- output, e.g. true, false

### parse_tag
Parse a tag string into a frozenset of Tag instances. tag: The tag to parse, e.g. "py3-none-any". validate_order: Check whether compressed tag set components ar
wraps packaging.tags.parse_tag
- parameter `tag` (string), e.g. "py3-none-any", "py2.py3-none-any", "cp39-cp39-win_amd64"
- parameter `validate_order` (boolean), e.g. true
- parameter `limit` (integer/null), e.g. 10, 5
- output, e.g. ["py3-none-any"], ["py2-none-any", "py3-none-any"], ["cp39-cp39-win_amd64"]

### generate_generic_tags
Generate generic interpreter tags. interpreter: The name of the interpreter, e.g. 'cp39'. abis: Iterable of compatible ABIs, e.g. ['cp39', 'abi3']. platforms: I
wraps packaging.tags.generic_tags
- parameter `interpreter` (null/string), e.g. "py39", "pypy38", "graalpy310"
- parameter `abis` (array/null), e.g. ["cp39", "abi3"], ["pp38"], ["gpy310"]

Generate interpreter-compatible tags for a Python version. python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the compatible version of Python, e.g. [3, 8

### canonicalize_package_name
Normalize a package name to its canonical form. name: The package name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonica
wraps packaging.utils.canonicalize_name
- parameter `name` (string), e.g. "Django", "oslo.concurrency", "requests"
- parameter `validate` (boolean), e.g. true
- output, e.g. "django", "oslo-concurrency", "requests"

### check_normalized_package_name
Check if a name is already in normalized form. name: The project name to check for normalization -> true if the name is normalized, false otherwise.
wraps packaging.utils.is_normalized_name
- parameter `name` (string), e.g. "requests", "Django", "-not-legal"
- output, e.g. true, false

### canonicalize_version_string
Return a canonical form of a version string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zero
wraps packaging.utils.canonicalize_version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0.1", "1.0.0", "1.4.0.0.0"
- parameter `strip_trailing_zero` (boolean), e.g. false
- output, e.g. "1.0.1", "1", "1.0.0"

### parse_wheel_filename
Parse a wheel filename into its components. filename: The name of the wheel file, e.g. 'foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl' -> {'name': 'foo', 'version': '1.0', 'build': 
wraps packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename
- parameter `filename` (string), e.g. "foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl", "bar-2.1.0.post1-cp38-cp38m-win_amd64.whl", "baz-1.0.0-1-py3-none-any.whl"
- output, e.g. {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0", "build": [], "tags": ["py3-none-any"]}, {"name": "bar", "version": "2.1.0.post1", "build": [], "tags": ["cp38-cp38m-win_amd64"]}, {"name": "baz", "version": "1.0.0", "build": [1, ""], "tags": ["py3-none-any"]}

### parse_sdist_filename
Parse an sdist filename into its components. filename: The name of the sdist file, e.g. 'foo-1.0.tar.gz' -> {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0"}.
wraps packaging.utils.parse_sdist_filename
- parameter `filename` (string), e.g. "foo-1.0.tar.gz", "bar-2.5.0.zip", "test-package-1.2.3.tar.gz"
- output, e.g. {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0"}, {"name": "bar", "version": "2.5.0"}, {"name": "test-package", "version": "1.2.3"}

### parse_version_string
Parse the given version string.
wraps packaging.version.parse
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0.0", "2.1.3.dev1", "1.0.0-alpha.1"
- output, e.g. "1.0.0", "2.1.3.dev1", "1.0.0a1"

Give types to their parameters and outputs.

Step 1: find the kinds of values this library works with. Look at the example values: strings that follow a format or name a specific kind of thing (for example an email address, a date, an identifier) are a kind of value. Give each kind a CamelCase type name, such as `EmailAddress`.
Step 2: give every parameter and every output a type.
- Use the same type for every parameter and output that holds the same kind of value in the same format, across all tools. Two things have the same type only if a value of one can be used as the other.
- Most string parameters hold one of the kinds from step 1. Use plain `string` only for free text that fits no kind.
- A list of values of one type is written `list[TypeName]`.
- An output that is an object can list which of its fields have a type. Leave out the other fields.
- Flags and counts get a plain JSON type: boolean, integer or number.

Reply with one JSON object, types first:
{"types": [{"name": "TypeName", "description": "what it is, with one example value"}],
 "tools": {"tool_name": {"parameters": {"param": "TypeName"}, "output": "TypeName"},
           "other_tool": {"parameters": {"items": "list[TypeName]", "strict": "boolean"}, "output": {"fields": {"name": "OtherType", "all": "list[TypeName]"}}}}}
Include every tool and every parameter.
